rows.definition: the repo's core rhetorical device - an explicit statement of what a claim does NOT cover, placed next to the claim so it cannot be overread - used as a heading in 74+ docs under four drifting spellings (honest fence / honesty fence / honest boundary / honesty gate) with no definition anywhere and no code symbol
gaps: define it once in the glossary, pick ONE spelling, and (ideally) name it in code where fences are machine-checked
the four spellings are a disambiguation-scorecard family waiting to happen - naming it here is the prerequisite

rows.definition: the recurring section (54 docs) that states what a feature deliberately does not attempt - the scope-declaration counterpart of the honest fence (which guards a specific claim) - never defined as a term
gaps: glossary entry drawing the scope-vs-fence line; today readers must infer the difference from usage

rows.definition: the line between what the kernel verifies and what it merely receives from an untrusted agent - a heading in 33 docs and the load-bearing idea of the whole system, with no code identifier and no glossary definition
gaps: the glossary's agent entry gestures at it; give the boundary itself a definition and a stable anchor

rows.definition: the recurring doc section (31 docs) recording which claims are proven vs open for a feature - readers meet it constantly, but which ledger file it denotes (if any) is never stated and no code writes a thing by this name
gaps: either bind the term to the real ledger artifact it summarizes or define it as a doc-section convention - today it reads like a system component that does not exist

rows.definition: the section (29 docs) pointing at the artifact/command a reader can run to verify a claim themselves - fak's evidence-over-assertion convention, unnamed and undefined
gaps: define the convention once (what qualifies as ground truth: a runnable command or a committed artifact) and link it from the doc templates

rows.definition: the criteria a claim/feature must meet to move up a maturity rung - a heading in 22 docs (plus 'Promotion rule' in 10) with no code symbol and no definition, despite gating being fak's favorite mechanism
gaps: define gate-vs-rule (or unify them) and anchor next to the maturity/support-maturity docs the sections gate

rows.definition: used in 45 docs for the latency-critical code route (decode loop, gateway serve path) - borrowed jargon everyone assumes, but WHICH paths are the hot paths is never enumerated, so the term cannot be checked

rows.definition: the ordered best-to-worst verdict scale every scorecard defines for its rows (crystal..undocumented, explicit..latent) - the shared pattern is used by 8+ docs as a heading but is named nowhere as the reusable concept it is
